name: Veda
description: BoringVault platform that runs onchain yield vaults. Users deposit into a vault through its Teller and withdraw instantly or through a queue. An agent can use the Veda API for vault data, withdraw queue reads and strategist calldata.

offchainApis.name: Veda API
offchainApis.use: List vaults for your tenant (GET /v1/vaults), read merkle roots (GET /v1/vaults/{chain}/{vault}/roots), read the withdraw queue (GET /v1/vaults/{chain}/{vault}/withdraw-queue), get swap quotes and build swap transactions (POST /v1/swap/quote, /v1/swap/market, /v1/swap/limit), and build strategist calldata (POST /v1/tx-builder/api/execute/...). Send the key as a Bearer token.

actions.name: read withdraw queue
actions.how: Call GET /v1/vaults/{chain}/{vault_address}/withdraw-queue with a bearer key. Filter by user or block when needed.

actions.name: deposit into vault
actions.description: Deposit an asset and receive vault shares
actions.how: Use the vault Teller deposit function on the vault chain. Get the vault and Teller addresses from the Veda console or GET /v1/vaults. Approve the asset first.

actions.name: withdraw from vault
actions.description: Withdraw shares instantly or through the queue
actions.how: Use Teller withdraw when buffer liquidity is available. Otherwise request a queued withdrawal through the BoringQueue.

risks: Vault contracts are per vault and not published in the public docs. Verify the Teller and Accountant addresses for each vault before sending funds.
The Accountant sets the share price and can pause updates when values move outside bounds. Deposits and withdrawals can stop.
Strategists move vault funds only through Merkle verified actions. A bad Merkle root or strategist can still lose funds.
Some vaults enforce share lock periods, so a withdrawal can wait.
The API needs a key and access is granted per tenant.
notes: Veda does not publish official contract addresses in its public docs, so none are listed. Contract roles from the docs: BoringVault holds funds, Teller handles deposits and withdrawals, Accountant publishes the exchange rate, Manager checks strategy actions against a Merkle tree, and BoringQueue handles delayed withdrawals. The chain list comes from DefiLlama and is not confirmed by Veda docs.
